svg.title: Two distinct counts satisfy the same total, sum of squares and population variance
svg.desc: Given total twelve, sum of squares sixty and population variance six, the positive integer count n must satisfy sixty over n minus the square of twelve over n equals six. Multiplying by n squared gives six n squared minus sixty n plus one hundred forty-four equals zero. Factorisation gives count four or count six. For count four, the mean is three and variance sixty over four minus three squared is six. The moment bound sixty at least thirty-six holds; example records one, one, three and seven have the required totals. For count six, the mean is two and variance sixty over six minus two squared is six. The bound sixty at least twenty-four holds; example records zero, zero, one, one, three and seven have the required totals. Both counts are valid for unrestricted real observations. Additional conditions must be checked for each candidate; one example witness is not a claim of uniqueness.
